newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Aznar sees more jobs created in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aznar sees more jobs created in 1997.

text.p: Spain's Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said on Thursday he expected new jobs would grow faster in 1997 than in 1996, thanks to the economic recovery and a recent labour deal between employers and unions.

"This outlook, with an economic pickup, low inflation and interest rates, and the labour deal is the best outlook to accelerate the creation of new jobs. If in the previous year we had around 200,000 new jobs, this year will be better," Aznar told reporters at a news conference.
"Employment data has been very good in March and it will also be good in April, in my opinion," he said.
Spain's unions and employers finished drafting an agreement on labour reforms in April and expect to sign the deal next Monday.
The government will then study ways of converting the proposals into legislation and Aznar added that a draft of the law should be ready by mid-May.
